article_paragraphs: Bosch has unveiled the latest generation of its popular Active Line Plus electric bicycle motor, bringing more power, less weight, and a significantly smaller footprint to one of the company’s most widely used drive systems.

The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.
And while it isn’t Bosch’s most powerful motor, the upgrades are fairly substantial.

The new Active Line Plus now produces up to 600 watts of peak power and 60 Nm of torque, along with a maximum pedal assistance level of 340%. That’s enough to give riders a healthy boost when accelerating away from traffic lights or climbing hills, without necessarily turning their everyday commuter into an overpowered mountain bike.
Like its predecessor, the motor is designed for Class 1 electric bicycles in the US, providing pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) without a throttle.

Remember, the Active Line motor is the drive system model that many e-bike companies use for their modestly performing e-bikes . It gives good power and control, combined with all the tech we’ve come to expect from Bosch, but it isn’t the motor e-bike makers use when they need an electric mountain bike to scale a steep mountainous trail.
Perhaps even more interesting than the increased power is what Bosch has done to the motor’s physical design.
The company developed a new two-stage gearbox that helps reduce the motor’s overall volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) off its weight.

title: The Pedego Element 2 eBike — CleanTechnica Tested
raw_summary: Pedego was one of the earliest companies to see the promise of ebikes and to build them at scale. It sales model was based around developing retail stores hosting both sales and rental options for customers. It was a great option, as it let prospective buyers see Pedego’s various ebikes in person, rent a bike for a day, and even pick it up in person. When ebikes moved into the mass market, Pedego was slow to adapt, and as a result, its $4,000 ebikes felt expensive and uncompetitive . Its retail stores were compelling and it felt like the company had a solid foothold in the market, so we were excited when Pedego reached out about the more affordable $2,195 Pedego Element 2.

It was a great option, as it let prospective buyers see Pedego’s various ebikes in person, rent a bike for a day, and even pick it up in person.

When ebikes moved into the mass market, Pedego was slow to adapt, and as a result, its $4,000 ebikes felt expensive and uncompetitive . Its retail stores were compelling and it felt like the company had a solid foothold in the market, so we were excited when Pedego reached out about the more affordable $2,195 Pedego Element 2.
Disclaimer: Pedego provided the Element 2 to the author for the purposes of this review.

We were excited to put the model through its paces to see how the company had improved its bikes for the masses and to see if they had cut any corners to achieve the lower pricing that they’re now able to offer. Assembly for the Pedego Element 2 was straightforward. It needed pedals, the handlebars to be mounted to the stem, and a few other odds and ends. But all told, it was very easy and straightforward to get it from the box to being street ready.

Hitting the streets, we found the low-step frame to be extremely comfortable, with an attractive colorway in its satin finish paint. Ours came in a sand color that’s extremely attractive and looks modern with the black accents on the bike.

The Element 2 has an integrated rack to which Pedego fitted a set of panniers for us that make it just the ultimate cargo bike right out of the box. We loaded this up with some groceries on a neighborhood run to pick up some food for dinner and found it to be more than capable of both getting down the hill loaded up with groceries and, obviously back to the house.

Taking it on a run down to the beach, the Pedego is a breeze and feels very confident, especially with its oversized knobby tires. Their larger volume gives it a bit of extra cushion and complements the front suspension fork, making for a very comfortable and confident ride whether you’re on the road or on a short bit of dirt.

On that note, don’t let the knobby tires and suspension fork fool you into thinking this is an all-terrain machine. While it can handle the occasional stint on the dirt, it was never designed to excel in off-road adventures.

title: A Rare 1993 Panoz Roadster V8 – An American-Made Caterham Killer
raw_summary: This is a 1993 Panoz Roadster, and amazingly, it has just 695 miles on the odometer since it was new. One of the reasons for this is that this car was built for company founder Dan Panoz as his personal car, it was then largely used for PR and promotional duties. The Panoz Roadster was one of the most unusual, and capable, low-volume sports cars in production in the United States in the mid-1990s. It had a chassis designed by Frank Costin, a body designed by former Porsche stylist Freeman Thomas, and it had the kind of sharp, intuitive handling of cars like the Caterham 7 .
summary: This is a 1993 Panoz Roadster, and amazingly, it has just 695 miles on the odometer since it was new. One of the reasons for this is that this car was built for company founder Dan Panoz as his personal car, it was then largely used for PR and promotional duties.
article_paragraphs: This is a 1993 Panoz Roadster, and amazingly, it has just 695 miles on the odometer since it was new. One of the reasons for this is that this car was built for company founder Dan Panoz as his personal car, it was then largely used for PR and promotional duties.

The Panoz Roadster was one of the most unusual, and capable, low-volume sports cars in production in the United States in the mid-1990s. It had a chassis designed by Frank Costin, a body designed by former Porsche stylist Freeman Thomas, and it had the kind of sharp, intuitive handling of cars like the Caterham 7 .

Panoz Auto Development only built 44 examples of its original Roadster between 1992 and 1995, and 176 of the aluminum-framed “AIV Roadster” that replaced it. Both used Ford Mustang running gear, and unusually, the model line began when Dan Panoz bought the rights to an Irish sports car whose manufacturer was going into receivership.
Panoz Auto Development only built 44 examples of its original Roadster between 1992 and 1995, and 176 of the aluminum-framed “AIV Roadster” that replaced it. Image courtesy of Panoz Auto Development.

Dan Panoz founded his namesake company in 1989 with backing from his father, Don, who’d made his fortune in pharmaceuticals and drug delivery, including the wildly successful transdermal nicotine patch for those wanting to quit smoking.

In 1988, Dan approached the Thompson Manufacturing Company of Wexford, which had been building the TMC Costin since 1983. The Costin was a sports car, essentially a Lotus Seven rival, with a chassis designed by legendary British engineer Frank Costin.

TMC was going into receivership, so Dan bought the rights and shipped its jigs, drawings and two sets of parts to Georgia. His first workshop was a former state salt shed. Two TMC men came too. The engineer soon flew home, unhappy that the car’s original 1.6 liter engine was to make way for a Ford V8, but the head fabricator Mick Murphy stayed on long-term.

Dan wanted the reliability that most small-volume sports cars lacked, so he used a complete Mustang driveline – including the engine, clutch, cooling system, Borg-Warner T-5 five-speed, as well as the rear axle and brakes. article_paragraphs: A hybrid Toyota minivan is easily one of the most rational vehicles you could get , but the automaker has issued a recall on its current model that puts a fly in that perfect-family-car ointment. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration report on a recall submitted last Tuesday, Toyota is recalling 228,367 Siennas from model years 2022 to 2026, built from September 16, 2021 through July 20 of this year. The current, hybrid-only version of the Sienna came on the scene for the 2021 model year, so it looks like those first model year cars aren't affected.

Per the report, the issue has to do with "certain recliner assemblies by a certain supplier during a certain production period equipped with a seat containing a certain seat belt pretensioner by a certain supplier." That's a direct quote from the NHTSA report, by the way.

Look, I know it's a serious safety issue and I'm sure that passage was vetted by many, many Toyota lawyers, but it's always funny to read official legal stuff like that written with the same tone as that one friend dishing gossip at brunch with feigned discretion after one too many mimosas.

The defect has to do with current-gen Siennas equipped with two captain's chairs in the middle row (read: seven-passenger models). These seats can recline and have seat belts that tighten in the event of a crash. Toyota discovered that in certain frontal collisions, the load produced by the seat belt pretensioner can cause "oscillation" in the recliner mechanism, in turn causing the seat backs to potentially move around during the crash. No bueno for occupant safety.

Toyota apparently discovered the flaw last year when it was doing prototype sled testing for a new second-row seat and seat belt design for a future vehicle, and has since been doing additional tests, even recovering second-row seat assemblies from the field to see how recliner mechanisms have held up over time in the real world. The report goes on to say that Toyota does not have a real estimate as to how many of the 228,000 or so Siennas involved actually have the defect (the "1%" reported at the top of the report is essentially a placeholder). According to the company, there have been no Field Technical Reports or warranty claims related to this defect.

As a no-charge fix, "the majority of involved vehicles" will get an updated version of the software that controls the seat belt pretensioner. About 200 Siennas equipped with the Mobility as a Service Package, meanwhile, will get new seat backs with a different recliner mechanism.

article_paragraphs: HARTFORD, Connecticut — Today, Sierra Club Connecticut, local environmental justice leaders, the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America, and state elected officials hosted a Press Conference on Connecticut’s High Asthma Rates in the Legislative Office Building.

Hartford ranked eighth in the Asthma and Allergy Foundation’s rankings of “ Asthma Capitals ” due to the city’s higher asthma rates and related deaths. Pollution from fossil fuel plants and systems, like the Capitol Area System, are heavy contributors to poor air quality and asthma risk in Connecticut.

A former co-generation power plant purchased by the State of Connecticut in 2022, the Capitol Area System requires extensive repair in order to continue providing heating and cooling to state and private buildings along its two mile loop, including the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) and the Appellate Court.

The Capitol Area System currently runs on methane gas to heat and cool the over a dozen buildings. Sierra Club is urging the State of Connecticut to lead by example and commit to a fossil fuel free, 100 percent renewable solution.

“It is beyond upsetting to see Hartford once again reach the near top of the Asthma Capitals list,” said Alycia Jenkins, Sierra Club Connecticut Organizer . “For generations, we have seen first hand here in our city how poor air quality is making our children, elders, and neighbors sicker. Now is the time for Connecticut to correct course and better address the air pollution from power plants and vehicles that is poisoning our air and worsening public health.”

“Clean air is not a luxury. It is essential to our health,” said Sen. Saud Anwar, a practicing pulmonary physician. “Air pollution puts us all at risk, but especially our children, seniors and people living with asthma. We know the harm, and we have the tools to do better. It is time to act.”

“This is a wakeup call for Connecticut policymakers and advocates. We need to do more to adopt asthma protective policies, especially in our urban communities,” said Dr. Mark Mitchell, environmental and public health physician .

“Policy makers have the power to make changes to save and improve lives and reduce asthma-related costs to society,” said Silva Sedrakian, Executive Director of Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America, New England Chapter .

While its performance figures—1064 horsepower, 217-mph top speed, 1345 pounds of downforce—only seem possible due to divine intervention, it's really the folks at Aston Martin, with input from the company's F1 team, who deserve the kudos.

A Mercedes-AMG-sourced twin-turbo V-8 acts as the base of the Valhalla's ultra-powerful plug-in hybrid powertrain, aided by two electric motors in the front and one integrated into the eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Torque-vectoring all-wheel drive and active aerodynamics in the front and rear help the Valhalla stick like flypaper. It might sound like you need an FIA Super License to get the most out of Aston's road-legal racecar, but that's where the Valhalla's magic truly lies—it's approachable enough to make even novices feel godlike at the racetrack.

article_paragraphs: For the billionaire who has always wondered what it's like to feel the wind rushing through their new hair plugs at 217 mph, Aston Martin has announced a new topless version of its utterly bonkers Valhalla supercar, the Valhalla Spider . It'll debut at the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, and despite the name, rich arachnophobes can rest easy knowing the Valhalla Spider comes with a black fabric roof in most markets, or an optional carbon fiber hard top that's standard on U.S. market cars to keep the elements out when necessary.

The Valhalla Spider is powered by the same twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter flat-plane crank V8 paired with a plug-in hybrid system, all of which produces a combined output of 1,064 horsepower and 811 pound-feet of torque — the same as the Valhalla coupe. The Spider also gets two front axle-mounted motors and one motor integrated into the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission, with no mechanical connection between the front and rear axles.

Differences between the Spider and the coupe include a taller intake snorkel, a clip-in wind deflector that stores in the sills, and a revised electronic stability program and active aero to handle roof-on or roof-off 200-mph+ runs. With the standard fabric top fitted, though, its top speed is limited to a rather pedestrian 124 mph. To go faster, you'll need to go topless or opt for that carbon roof.

Going topless hasn't forced Aston to drop the Valhalla's dihedral doors. In fact, chopping the top made getting in and out a bit easier — and not just when the top is removed. According to Aston Martin, "Valhalla Spider retains its signature carbon fiber dihedral doors, preserving the sense of theater; now with refined kinematics for smoother operation and a transition to a frameless design. A small increase in the curvature of the door glass top edge also improves entry and exit when the roof is fitted."

A new carbon fiber Touring Seat comes standard on the Valhalla Spider, which is also meant to enhance ease of entry and exit with the roof on, though the original carbon fiber seat form the Valhalla Coupe can be optioned at no extra cost for better support.

Despite losing its roof, the Valhalla Spider still uses a version of the coupe's bespoke carbon fiber tub designed and engineered by Aston Martin Performance Technologies, the consulting arm of the company's F1 team. The Valhalla Coupe was priced around $1 million when it debuted in 2024, but considering the giant leap in inflation and the naturally pricier nature of convertibles, this one will likely be much more. And if you have to ask about the Valhalla Spider's price tag, you absolutely cannot afford one.

raw_summary: Over the coming year, renewables’ share of total generating capacity will grow from 37.7% to 40.4%, surpassing that of natural gas and outstripping nuclear capacity fivefold, according to new data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign. article_paragraphs: Over the coming year, renewables’ share of total generating capacity will grow from 37.7% to 40.4%, surpassing that of natural gas and outstripping nuclear capacity fivefold, according to new data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign.

According to the EIA’s latest “ Electric Power Monthly ” report (with data through August 31, 2026), renewably generated electricity during the first two-thirds of 2026 was 10.2% greater year over year. The growth was led by utility-scale [>1 MW] solar (up 20.0%), small-scale solar (up 12.0%), wind (up 7.8%), hydropower (up 4.2%), and geothermal (up 3.8%).

From January to August 2026, wind produced 333,367 gigawatt-hours (GWh) – 10.6% of total US electrical generation – while utility-scale and small-scale solar combined produced 329,119 GWh (10.5%), hydropower produced 180,940 GWh (5.7%), biomass produced 29,917 GWh (1.0%), and geothermal produced 10,766 GWh (0.34%).
By comparison, the electrical output of US natural gas and nuclear power plants grew more slowly – by just 2.6% and 1.3%, respectively. Electricity produced by US coal plants fell by 8.7%.

During the first eight months of 2026, the combination of wind and solar, including small-scale solar, accounted for almost 21.1% of domestic electricity production, with wind at 10.6% and solar at nearly 10.5%.
During the first two-thirds of this year, wind and solar combined produced 44.4% more electricity than coal and 24.8% more than nuclear.
Through the end of August, the mix of all renewables, including biomass, accounted for 28.1% of total US electrical generation – up from 26.2% a year earlier.

Between September 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, the installed capacity of utility-scale solar increased by 27,141.7 MW, while that of small-scale solar and wind grew by 6,526.1 MW and 9,979.1 MW (including 800 MW of offshore wind), respectively. The combined capacity of all renewable energy sources, including hydropower, biomass, and geothermal, expanded by 43,497.9 MW.

Now, though, another brand thinks it can hit the Bavarians where their hold is strongest. Triumph has revamped the Tiger 1200 lineup to hit BMW where it hurts, and the Brits have a solid shot of making a real mark.

The Tiger 1200 line is still split into its four component models — GT Pro, Rally Pro, GT Explorer, and Rally Explorer — but Triumph has streamlined things between the four bikes to make their differences clearer. Every model now comes with a 19 inch front wheel and a 17 out back, and all four get trick self-lowering Showa suspension with 7.9 inches of travel front and rear — until you come to a stop, at which point the system drops the bike almost 1.2 inches.

Triumph says the seat height, with a low seat installed and the self-lowering suspension active, can get as low as 31.1 inches at a stop. That's impressively low for a big adventure bike, and over an inch shorter than the competing R 1300 GS. On top of the trick suspension updates, Triumph has updated the Tiger's rider display — a new 7-inch display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto now standard. There's also the updated 1,160cc three-cylinder engine with a redesigned cylinder head, new pistons, lighter intake and exhaust valves, and revised gear ratios for first, second, and third. The engine now makes 155.8 horsepower (up from 147 hp). Triumph also claims that the new Tiger 1200 has more torque down low, which improves slow-speed performance.

If you're a bit confused by all the Tiger 1200's available variants, here's how Triumph differentiates them: GT bikes get cast wheels, while the Rally bikes get spokes. Rally bikes get an extra off-road ride mode and some engine protection. Explorer bikes get wider and taller handlebars and 7.9-gallon fuel tanks rather than the Pro bikes' 5.3-gallon units. Got all that?

Essentially, they're the same chassis, engine, and suspension across all models, but the Rally bikes get some dirt features, and Explorer bikes get the right gear for long tours . All four get Bosch radar front and rear, as well, to enable both adaptive cruise control and rear close-follow warnings — they're all competent tourers, big tank or no.

The best change for 2027 to my eye, though, is the appearance of the new Tiger 1200 lineup. The prior bikes were stuck in an awkward in-between period, where Triumph was in the process of ditching its long-lasting twin-headlight design but hadn't yet gone all-in on compact LED illumination. Now it has, and the Tiger looks all the better for it — that single center headlight below the light bar really works for me. It's functional, too, with corner lighting built into the central LED that illuminates when the rider leans.

title: GM is embracing hybrids now
raw_summary: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers. The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”
summary: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers. The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”
article_paragraphs: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers.

The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.”

The company said it is working with the U.S. Department of Energy to restructure a previously awarded Domestic Manufacturing Conversion Grant and direct those funds to future hybrid production at the Lansing factory. The company was awarded $500 million under the Biden administration to support converting a different factory in Lansing to produce electric vehicles, including hybrid, battery-electric, plug-in electric hybrid, and hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles. Those funds were never released, according to GM.
Today, GM assembles the gas-powered Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse, and GMC Acadia at the Lansing Delta Township factory, which produced a record 291,000 vehicles in 2025.

GM didn’t provide specifics on when it would begin producing and selling hybrid vehicles. But insiders told TechCrunch to expect hybrids across multiple brands rather than a single vehicle line. A Reuters report , citing anonymous sources, said the company plans to build hybrid versions of the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia at the factory.

Hybrids have become increasingly popular, thanks in part to rising gas prices. Customers also have more choices than ever before, with most automakers offering a range of hybrid and plug-in hybrid models. Toyota is the U.S. market leader in hybrid sales, followed by Honda. Ford has also gained considerable market share in hybrid sales in the past two years, selling some 228,000 hybrids in 2025.

But GM has been slow to adopt hybrids. Until recently, the company’s only electric-hybrid vehicle was the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray , which launched as a 2024 model. (GM sold 2,444 of those vehicles last year.) The E-Ray has since been discontinued; GM began deliveries of the hybrid Corvette ZR1X in March and next year will launch a hybrid Corvette Grand Sport X.

GM eschewed hybrids in favor of battery-electric vehicles. The automaker invested billions of dollars to shift its gas-powered portfolio to an all-electric one. That strategy has changed under the Trump administration with the end of the federal EV tax credit and slower-than-expected demand. GM hasn’t abandoned EVs completely, though it has seen EV sales fall year-over-year. The company still sells numerous battery-electric vehicles across its brands, including the Chevrolet Equinox EV, Blazer EV, and Cadillac Escalade IQ.

article_paragraphs: Re:Build, the Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator that spun out EV startup Slate Auto in 2023, has raised $2.1 billion

The company said Tuesday that it will use the funding to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups,” which will “ensure the most innovative products can be made in America for generations to come.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The funding round comes as increasing attention and capital is flowing to the idea of building up manufacturing and supply chains in the United States, especially as a hedge away from China.

“We started Re:Build because the deindustrialization of America is an economic failure and national security risk,” Re:Build co-founder Jeff Wilke said in a statement. “This capital allows Re:Build to go faster and further than would otherwise be possible, and build a great manufacturing business and a platform for American industrial leadership. The products and companies emerging from our ecosystem prove we can help restore America’s industrial might.”

General Catalyst’s CEO Hemant Taneja echoed those sentiments in a statement, saying, “General Catalyst has long believed that rebuilding American industrial capacity is one of the most important economic and national security imperatives of our time.”

Taneja added: “To compete with China, re-industrialize the U.S., and revitalize the towns and jobs that have been left behind, we need platform companies that can operate at genuine scale — and we need our innovation ecosystem to learn how to build hardware again.”

Founded in 2020, Re:Build bills itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen,” and it has numerous ties to Amazon. It was co-founded by Wilke, who was Amazon’s former commercial CEO. Wei Gao, a longtime Amazon VP and technical adviser to Bezos, is Re:Build’s chief digital and product officer. Multiple other Re:Build executives also worked for the e-commerce giant.

Re:Build claims to have “launched hundreds of products and production systems” over its six-year existence. The company tends to operate two ways: It enters partnerships with industrial companies to “design, engineer, and manufacture products at scale across verticals including aerospace and defense,” and it incubates startups in “critical, underserved markets.”

raw_summary: Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting more than 9,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity. article_paragraphs: Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting more than 9,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity.
Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026.
The recall is due to the risk of thermal propagation, or a battery fire, under certain conditions when charged to over 80% of its limit.

Volkswagen said in a safety recall report with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) that “certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation.”

While the root cause is unknown, Volkswagen urged owners to limit charging to 80%. Owners of affected vehicles received an email saying VW “intends to apply a temporary vehicle setting that limits charging to 80%,” unless they opted out by October 21.
In the letter sent to the NHTSA on October 23, Volkswagen Group of America said it was issuing a recall affecting 9,048 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles model years 2024 to 2025.
The safety recall follows Audi’s Product Safety Committee being informed of battery thermal events involving other Volkswagen Group EVs that use the same batteries as the Audi Q4 E-Tron.

Following an internal investigation, Audi found the same battery and production characteristics as the impacted VW Group vehicles. Audi said the majority of these were produced for the North American market.

raw_title: The KTM X-Bow Is Finally Coming To American Roads
title: The KTM X-Bow Is Finally Coming To American Roads
raw_summary: The KTM X-Bow has been around since 2008, but there has never been a road-legal production version available in the United States — until now. KTM X-Bow has just announced the X-Bow GT-XA, a U.S. road version of its nimble sports car. The spun-off Austrian manufacturer plans to build 30 cars for the model's first year of production, but there is just one hiccup. The GT-XA has yet to be approved for U.S. road use. KTM X-Bow stated that its exclusive U.S. partner, Carbon Yard, is working to secure U.S. road legalization for the GT-XA. Regardless of how long that takes, the factory in Graz, Austria, will be assembling sports cars with a delivery target of 2027 in mind. Prospective buyers can place reservations for $50,000, which will remain fully refundable until the GT-XA becomes road legal. KTM X-Bow has yet to announce technical specifications or a final MSRP for the U.S.-spec two-seater, but is anticipating a $490,000 price tag.

KTM X-Bow has yet to announce technical specifications or a final MSRP for the U.S.-spec two-seater, but is anticipating a $490,000 price tag.

The X-Bow was forever changed when it went racing in 2015. KTM produced a factory racing version for GT4 competition , which necessitated a closed cockpit to fit the regulations. Engineers fitted a canopy over the cockpit because the existing monocoque made doors impractical. The canopy would make its street-legal X-Bow debut in 2022 with the GT-XR, the likely basis for the upcoming GT-XA. According to X-Bow, the U.S.-spec version will feature a front-axle lift system to make it easier to pull into driveways.

The canopy undoubtedly expanded the X-Bow's customer base, but it strayed from the car's initial ethos. The 2,760-pound GT-XR is over 1,000 pounds heavier than the original open-cockpit model. It might not be a true fighter jet canopy, as KTM X-Bow advertises, but I wouldn't want to be inside a canopied X-Bow if it flipped on a public road. I'm not sure I could squeeze my way out of one of those tiny windows. At a race track, at least the marshals are there to respond and help you escape if you end up trapped in an overturned X-Bow.

I don't want to sound too critical of creature comforts, but the original X-Bow was a breath of fresh air for the realm of enthusiast sports cars from a very unusual source. An Austrian motorcycle manufacturer produced a lightweight, open-cockpit sports car constructed around a carbon fiber monocoque. The partnership with dominant single-seat builder Dallara led many to think of the X-Bow as a street-legal, formula-style race car, but its raw agility could easily be described as a four-wheeled motorcycle. The GT-XR just isn't that. I guess I should also mention that, after KTM's massive restructuring , the X-Bow was spun off into a separate company with different owners than the bike maker.

raw_title: This Mid-Engine V8 Geo Metro Is The Ultimate Evolution Of 'LS Swap All The Things'
title: This Mid-Engine V8 Geo Metro Is The Ultimate Evolution Of 'LS Swap All The Things
raw_summary: LS swaps are so common they've become a cliché. We've seen them in everything from Miatas and classic turbocharged Chevy Suburbans to Suzuki kei cars . That means it's perfectly reasonable to drop the big V8 into its Suzuki-made cousin, this Geo Metro currently for sale on Cars & Bids , right? Wait, what do you mean it won't fit in the engine bay where the 1.0-liter inline-3 used to go? That's okay, just rip out the back seats and put it there instead. Of course, it's not nearly that simple. The most obvious visual clue that something's not normal about this car is that the rear quarter panels have been completely rebuilt. The larger wheels, sourced from a Cadillac DeVille, have been pushed beyond the rear corners of the car, giving it an awkward raked appearance. Air scoops have been carved into each side to feed cool air into the rear half of the car, which has been sealed off, hopefully keeping any errant fumes from entering the cabin.

That means it's perfectly reasonable to drop the big V8 into its Suzuki-made cousin, this Geo Metro currently for sale on Cars & Bids , right?

Wait, what do you mean it won't fit in the engine bay where the 1.0-liter inline-3 used to go? That's okay, just rip out the back seats and put it there instead.

Of course, it's not nearly that simple. The most obvious visual clue that something's not normal about this car is that the rear quarter panels have been completely rebuilt. The larger wheels, sourced from a Cadillac DeVille, have been pushed beyond the rear corners of the car, giving it an awkward raked appearance. Air scoops have been carved into each side to feed cool air into the rear half of the car, which has been sealed off, hopefully keeping any errant fumes from entering the cabin.

While the Metro is a small car, the 5.3-liter LS4 V8 somehow fits back here, as well as the four-speed automatic transmission. This version of the LS almost certainly came from a front-wheel-drive sedan of the early 2000s , like the Chevy Impala or Monte Carlo SS, the Pontiac Grand Prix GXP, or even the Buick Lacrosse Super. GM already solved all the packaging problems of a transverse LS before this swap was dreamed up. Then, all the builder had to do was cut, widen, and reinforce the Metro's body to accommodate the existing drivetrain and subframe, as well as to handle its 303 horsepower and 323 pound-feet of torque. The car originally made just 55 hp, so it likely needed all the help it could get.

As part of this build, the cooling system obviously needed to be redesigned, since putting it in front of the engine wouldn't help much in this unique application. A large radiator sits tucked behind the rear bumper, which now looks like a slice of Swiss cheese that allows air to flow through it. Although the car has a recent paint job changing the color to red, the front and rear bumpers remain unpainted, just like the original Metro. There's little original about this LS-swapped Geo (rebadged as a Chevy, like the later Metros were), but somehow that design choice just feels right.

With a V8 stuffed in the rear, the fuel tank needed to move someplace else. The builder took a cue from the VW Beetle, putting the tank in the front of the car where the original engine used to be. This location was good enough for the Porsche 911 , and it's a racing fuel cell, so that must make it at least a little bit safe.

If the Ford Fiesta Shogun is too common for you ( six examples still survive, and you know Jay Leno isn't giving up his), this one-off mid-engine V8 Geo Metro might scratch the same strange itch, and it is currently for sale on Cars & Bids . While it's currently registered in Illinois, the listing does note that, "Due to the modifications performed to this Metro, it may not pass emissions testing in some states." I have a feeling that anyone interested in a V8 Metro is less interested in emissions and fuel economy than in speed and the absolute awesomeness of a build like this.

raw_title: Flock Cameras Are Being Covered With Garbage Bags As Contracts With The Wildly Unpopular Mass Surveillance Company Are Terminated
title: Flock Cameras Are Being Covered With Garbage Bags As Contracts With The Wildly Unpopular Mass Surveillance Company Are Terminated
raw_summary: As the number of cities that have dropped Flock camera contracts has been rising steeply, some of those cities have been unsure how to stop the surveillance that come standard with the now-installed camera hardware. More and more places have resorted to putting trash bags over the cameras, reports WREG News Channel 3 , as a temporary measure to prevent cameras from tracking your every move until they can be removed properly. It's almost like the trash is taking itself out. While some concerned citizens have resorted to vandalism to remove the unwanted cameras, the correct way to make them go away is to work through the proper channels, attend town meetings, and get the communities you live in to decide to take them down themselves. They're much more likely to stay down that way. After all, police continue to misuse this "Big Brother" technology, either by accident or completely on purpose , and Flock customers have been dropping like flies with all the reports of errors and abuses continuing to pop up in the media.

More and more places have resorted to putting trash bags over the cameras, reports WREG News Channel 3 , as a temporary measure to prevent cameras from tracking your every move until they can be removed properly.
article_paragraphs: As the number of cities that have dropped Flock camera contracts has been rising steeply, some of those cities have been unsure how to stop the surveillance that come standard with the now-installed camera hardware. More and more places have resorted to putting trash bags over the cameras, reports WREG News Channel 3 , as a temporary measure to prevent cameras from tracking your every move until they can be removed properly. It's almost like the trash is taking itself out.

While some concerned citizens have resorted to vandalism to remove the unwanted cameras, the correct way to make them go away is to work through the proper channels, attend town meetings, and get the communities you live in to decide to take them down themselves. They're much more likely to stay down that way. After all, police continue to misuse this "Big Brother" technology, either by accident or completely on purpose , and Flock customers have been dropping like flies with all the reports of errors and abuses continuing to pop up in the media.

City governments can't just rip down Flock cameras on their own. They signed contracts with Flock Safety to get them in the first place, and often it's Flock that's responsible for installing, maintaining, and removing them. Unlike vandals, cities and towns have to abide by the terms of those contracts, and the law. But there's no law, or clause in the contract, that says they can't cover up the cameras, rendering them useless for surveilling the public until they can arrange for proper removal.

As they wait to remove the cameras permanently, more municipalities have resorted to the simple and oddly poetic solution of covering them with trash bags. Dayton, Ohio, first did this in May. Others have followed, such as Harrisburg, Arkansas, earlier in October after residents complained loudly that they didn't want them. Mayor Justin Kimble told WREG New Channel 3:

It's hard for me, because I come from law enforcement, and it's hard for me to say, man, I don't want to take this tool away from [law enforcement]. But if you have the majority of your community, me and my city council really need to listen to what the people want.
It's a rare, good politician who can set aside his personal feelings and put the desires of the community above his own.

Canceling a community's Flock service isn't as simple as canceling the streaming service that just got rid of all your favorite shows, though. Cities may contract with Flock for a specific period of time, and need to follow proper procedures to either cancel the contract or fulfill payment obligations while not using the service. The local governments don't want to knowingly breach the contracts, which would cost taxpayers more than just keeping the service in the first place.

It's also not as simple as public works departments shutting the cameras off themselves. Some have tried, only for Flock to turn them back on again, which is exactly what happened in Littleton, Massachusetts, reports the Lowell Sun . If they keep Flock out of the loop, they perceive the non-functional cameras as a problem, then "fix" them under the service contract, defeating the purpose of shutting them down until they can be permanently removed.

title: Mercedes has a Russell-sized problem and it is sharing responsibility
raw_summary: George Russell's form hit a new low at the United States Grand Prix, despite glimmers of progress in the Formula 1 grands prix shortly before then. In Austin, the Mercedes driver qualified over four tenths behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, slumping to an eighth-placed finish on Sunday while the 20-year-old took another step to the world title with a ninth win of 2026. There were some mitigating circumstances behind Russell's P8, as a five-second penalty on lap one dropped him behind McLaren's Oscar Piastri . Permanently, as it would transpire. But Mercedes boss Toto Wolff pointed out afterwards that that "doesn't make any difference to the underlying problem that we need to solve”.

In Austin, the Mercedes driver qualified over four tenths behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, slumping to an eighth-placed finish on Sunday while the 20-year-old took another step to the world title with a ninth win of 2026.
article_paragraphs: George Russell's form hit a new low at the United States Grand Prix, despite glimmers of progress in the Formula 1 grands prix shortly before then. In Austin, the Mercedes driver qualified over four tenths behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli, slumping to an eighth-placed finish on Sunday while the 20-year-old took another step to the world title with a ninth win of 2026.

There were some mitigating circumstances behind Russell's P8, as a five-second penalty on lap one dropped him behind McLaren's Oscar Piastri . Permanently, as it would transpire. But Mercedes boss Toto Wolff pointed out afterwards that that "doesn't make any difference to the underlying problem that we need to solve”.

It came despite a slight upturn in form following the summer break, like his Baku win, before the Russell-sized problems grew worse and worse heading into Texas. Other than a strong performance in Singapore sprint qualifying, taking second before crashing from the lead, he hasn't qualified higher than sixth - or higher than Antonelli - since Mercedes introduced its major Malaysia upgrade. Though, of course, he was on course for third at Sepang until a late engine failure.

Nevertheless, Russell isn’t having the best of times with the new package and looked bereft of ideas as to why things aren't clicking for him. But the prevailing theory is that the new-look W17, while demonstrably faster at its peak, has a much narrower performance window. Whether a matter of driving style or adaptation, when the car isn't in that sweet spot, Russell appears to be all at sea.

"George just struggled so much," Wolff said. "I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult. In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3 didn't work. He said: 'That goes on me.'
“In the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair. Why he didn't get past is [because they have] the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment."

Russell summed up his race as "six good laps, 50 bad laps", but was otherwise at a loss for words to explain his unravelling performances. "I want to understand why the pace was so bad in the first stint,” he said, now with a 123-point gap to Antonelli. “The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that was least of my worries after such a bad weekend.

"The potential is there, but the window is narrow. I mean, we saw it in Malaysia. I think he [Antonelli] was quickest in FP3 and then we qualified fourth and eighth. And then this weekend we were both up there in Q2, and then I was nowhere in Q3 and nowhere [in the race].

raw_title: Toyota Just Put All Its Trucks On Snow Tracks
title: Toyota Just Put All Its Trucks On Snow Tracks
raw_summary: The SEMA Show is where some of the wildest builds come out to play, and rising to the occasion this year is Toyota , which has slapped snow tracks onto all of its body-on-frame products to create what it calls the Snowhunter concepts. Yes, concepts, which means they likely aren't coming to a Toyota showroom any time soon, but it's still a fun exercise. Specifically, the Land Cruiser, 4Runner, Sequoia, Tacoma, and Tundra have been made to look like miniature tanks, all in the name of "winter exploration." On top of the tracks, common additions include Rigid lighting, TRD rear billet control arms, in-house lift components, and Predator steps that make getting in and out easier. (There's gotta be a better name for that last one.) They all get equipment to accommodate all the equipment that comes with arctic adventure. The SUVs all get a Prinsu roof rack with accessory panels plus a Thule Pulse 2 cargo box, while the pickups get bed-based rack systems: Toyota's TrailLift Pro bed system for the Tundra and a full-length bed rack with MOLLE panels on the Tacoma.

The add-ons have also been mildly tailored to fit each vehicle's purpose. The family-oriented Sequoia, for example, gets a front TRD skid plate, running boards, and the cargo box, whereas the rough-and-tumble Land Cruiser receives rock rails, skid plates, and a ski rack.

Of course, it all looks incredibly cool, which means they accomplish what I suspect was the real mission of these builds. They're all decked out in white snow-camo liveries and look like they could conquer blizzards of apocalyptic proportions. These Snowhunter concepts are indeed concepts for now, but you might recognize that name as a play on "Trailhunter," an off-road trim of Toyota trucks that is sold to the public.

Speaking as a Canadian, there's a decent subset of off-road customers that don't actually go off-roading in a recreational sense — they just want something that will get them to work easily during the two days a year most everybody else is urged to stay home. Snow tracks likely won't make it to production since they're not road legal in most jurisdictions, but toned-down Snowhunter trims of Toyota's beefiest rigs could be a hit in northern markets.

I’ve spent some time now riding the X7, and while it certainly isn’t the most refined electric dirt bike I’ve tested, there’s enough to like about what you’re getting for the money.
In fact, if you’re looking for a reasonably powerful electric dirt bike for recreational trail riding without spending several thousand dollars, this might be worth a closer look.

The Sykeruns X7 is a compact electric dirt bike featuring a 5,500W peak-rated motor, which translates to around 7.4 horsepower. That’s quite a bit of power for a bike at this price point of $1,699 , especially considering that many similarly priced electric two-wheelers are significantly less powerful. Oh, and for our readers, we’ve gotten you set up with a 20% discount. Just use code ELECTREK20 to drop the price down to an impressive $1,359!

Sykeruns claims a top speed of 57 mph (92 km/h), though since this is an off-road only bike, you’ll rarely get the chance to put that claim to the test. I certainly didn’t, as I didn’t have a long enough and flat enough stretch of trail where I felt comfortable hitting nearly highway speeds on a low-cost e-moto.

The battery is a 60V 27Ah pack, providing 1,620 Wh of capacity. Sykeruns claims up to 60 miles (96 km) of range, though as with virtually every electric dirt bike, your actual range will depend heavily on how aggressively you’re riding. Fast trail riding, steep climbs, and repeated hard acceleration can eat through battery capacity much more quickly than leisurely cruising. Suffice it to say that you’ll likely not see the 60 mile figure in real world scenarios, but that’s still a fairly large battery.

The bike rolls on a 17-inch front wheel and 14-inch rear wheel, both wrapped in knobby off-road tires. Hydraulic disc brakes handle stopping duties, while an inverted suspension fork and rear monoshock help smooth out the bumps.
At 143 lb (65 kg), the X7 isn’t exactly featherweight, but it’s also far from being a full-size electric motorcycle.

title: Korean police book 80 Tesla drivers over illegal FSD unlock devices
raw_summary: Seoul police have booked 80 people for using aftermarket devices to switch on Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” in cars that aren’t allowed to run it in South Korea. Officers also seized 21 of the devices. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case on Tuesday. It’s the largest enforcement action yet against the FSD “jailbreak” hardware that has spread through China, Europe, and Korea over the past year.

Officers also seized 21 of the devices. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case on Tuesday. It’s the largest enforcement action yet against the FSD “jailbreak” hardware that has spread through China, Europe, and Korea over the past year.
article_paragraphs: Seoul police have booked 80 people for using aftermarket devices to switch on Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” in cars that aren’t allowed to run it in South Korea. Officers also seized 21 of the devices.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case on Tuesday. It’s the largest enforcement action yet against the FSD “jailbreak” hardware that has spread through China, Europe, and Korea over the past year.

Police say the suspects either imported the unlock modules from Europe and China or made their own. One plugged a European-made unit into his own Tesla. Another, an IT worker, built his device with information he found on GitHub.
Suspects also swapped advice online on how to unlock FSD and how to stop the car from keeping any record that it had been activated.

They’re charged under Korea’s Motor Vehicle Management Act, which bans unauthorized software changes that can affect a vehicle’s safety. The penalty is up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won (about $15,000).

The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport asked police to look into it back in April after finding signs of unauthorized activation. A police official told Korea JoongAng Daily that “safety risks were confirmed,” including the possibility of FSD misreading driving conditions. The investigation is ongoing, with police consulting the ministry and the Korea Transportation Safety Authority on the technical side.

Tesla launched FSD (Supervised) in South Korea in late 2025, but only on US-built vehicles: Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck. Those cars are exempt from Korean safety certification under the Korea-US free trade agreement. The Model 3 and Model Y, which Tesla ships to Korea from Giga Shanghai, haven’t cleared Korea’s safety standards for the feature.
And those two models are the bulk of the fleet. Citing Carisyou Data Lab, Korea JoongAng Daily reports that 47,458 of the 229,311 Teslas on Korean roads as of August, or 20.7%, can legally use FSD.

title: Audi's New Digital Matrix Lights Project Turn Signals Onto The Road And Won't Blind Other Cars
raw_summary: Audi is known for its advanced lighting technology, and has been since it first introduced the concept of LED daytime running lights (DRLs) that are now basically a prerequisite for all new cars. Many of its recently updated models have customizable DRLs that offer owners a chance to choose between several different lighting designs for both the front and rear running lights. The new 2027 Audi Q9 offers that feature, but more importantly, it's the first U.S.-spec Audi model to feature the brand's digital matrix LED headlights and new projections, too. This is a technology that Audi has had for years now — nearly a decade, in fact — but U.S. regulations stupidly outlawed the brilliant technology on all cars in the country. This is the first Audi that's been programmed to meet the recently updated U.S. headlight requirements , while still providing functional matrix headlights.

article_paragraphs: Audi is known for its advanced lighting technology, and has been since it first introduced the concept of LED daytime running lights (DRLs) that are now basically a prerequisite for all new cars. Many of its recently updated models have customizable DRLs that offer owners a chance to choose between several different lighting designs for both the front and rear running lights. The new 2027 Audi Q9 offers that feature, but more importantly, it's the first U.S.-spec Audi model to feature the brand's digital matrix LED headlights and new projections, too.

This is a technology that Audi has had for years now — nearly a decade, in fact — but U.S. regulations stupidly outlawed the brilliant technology on all cars in the country. This is the first Audi that's been programmed to meet the recently updated U.S. headlight requirements , while still providing functional matrix headlights.

The tricks don't end there, though. On Q9s with the Prestige package, the car projects a solid white rhombus onto the ground beneath the front and rear doors that unfurls when the door opens, or when a cyclist or car is approaching to signal a passenger is getting out of the Q9. Of course, it also includes exit warning that uses the radar sensors in the rear bumper to detect approaching vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians, that can prevent doors form opening or stop a door that's already opening into the obstacle. In a scenario like that, the projection lights also display warnings to protect everyone involved.

Beyond those functions, the headlights and taillights also contain little projectors that shine turn arrows onto the road when the headlights are on, which is pretty friggin' neat. The curved OLED taillights are the first of their kind to appear on any road car, and will also display a hazard triangle when the hazard lights are activated, as well as offering drivers their choice of eight DRL signatures.

The matrix headlights use the camera mounted behind the rear-view mirror to scan the road ahead for other cars and road signs. When the driver has their high beams on, the car is able to create a gap in the high beam light projection that essentially creates a little box of darkness that follows any other cars or road signs ahead. This means the driver enjoys the increased illumination provided by having the high beams on, and all other road users don't end up getting blinded by them as a result.

To showcase the tech, Audi sent us journalists out into the darkness of the Utah desert at night time, where I was clearly able to see the benefit of the system. Especially on unlit rural roads, the Q9's high beams provided a significantly better field of illumination, and I was hardly able to detect the darker boxes that surrounded other cars, both oncoming traffic and lead traffic, as well as road signs, so as not to blind the driver. I think this will be a big improvement for all road users, as well as Audi owners.

The turn signal projections weren't super bright and visible in all scenarios, but they could prove to be a valuable safety feature. The scenarios Audi used to demonstrate their efficacy make a good case for the technology. If someone in a Q9 was parallel parked on a busy road, the Q9 driver could signal to indicate their desire to pull out, and since the arrows are projected out wider than the car, upcoming traffic can see the arrows on the road before they would otherwise be able to see the integral turn signal lights.

Digital matrix lights are standard on the Q9 Premium Plus trim and above, and standard on SQ9. The advanced turn signals are only included in the $4,750 Luxury package that also includes the powered doors on the SQ9, and they come included in the $14,700 Prestige package on the Q9. It's all really cool, and probably obscenely expensive to replace when they go wrong or get bonked in a busy parking lot, so maybe park at the back of the lot.

The 2027 Kia EV9 starts at $54,990, up a measly $90 from last year’s model. That’s for the base EV9 Light short-range trim, which uses a 76.1 kWh battery and delivers up to 230 miles of range.
Higher-priced trims, including the Light Long Range, Wind, Land, and GT-Line, use a larger 99.8 kWh battery that delivers up to 305 miles of range in RWD variants.
The Wind and Land trims have standard all-wheel-drive (AWD) and offer up to 283 miles of range, while the GT-Line is also AWD but offers slightly less range at 280 miles.
Kia’s dual-motor e-AWD system delivers up to 379 hp and 516 lb-ft of torque in the EV9 GT-Line, enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 4.5 seconds.
For the 2027 model, the EV9 Wind now comes with black-finish 19″ wheels and the Glossy Black exterior paint color as standard, and Wolf Gray paint is newly available as an option.
The 2027 EV9 Land now includes the Nightfall Edition Package, which was previously optional, as standard. It starts at $69,990, or $500 less than the 2026 Kia EV9 Land Nightfall Edition.

title: The role Friday practice played in Hamilton failing to achieve a podium at the US GP
raw_summary: Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why the podium narrowly eluded him in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix. The Ferrari driver started from fifth on the grid and jumped Isack Hadjar for fourth at lights out, despite being the only driver on used (soft) tyres for the opening stint.
summary: Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why the podium narrowly eluded him in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix. The Ferrari driver started from fifth on the grid and jumped Isack Hadjar for fourth at lights out, despite being the only driver on used (soft) tyres for the opening stint.
article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton has explained the reasons why the podium narrowly eluded him in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix.
The Ferrari driver started from fifth on the grid and jumped Isack Hadjar for fourth at lights out, despite being the only driver on used (soft) tyres for the opening stint.

But Hamilton lost 0.277s per lap to team-mate Charles Leclerc during that stint, as well as 0.422s to Max Verstappen , with the pair on new soft tyres. Those few seconds corresponded to the time the Briton was missing to beat Verstappen to third at the end of the Austin race – and perhaps surpass Leclerc for second.
The main reason for that early lack of pace, according to the seven-time world champion, was his suboptimal set-up in the opening stint – the consequence of pursuing wrong avenues in free practice.
“I was lacking pace in the first two stints, basically. I just couldn't turn the car,” Hamilton said.
“Ultimately, it all kind of started on Friday. Wrong set-up really for FP1 and went the wrong direction in FP2, reverted back and got to a better place in FP3.

“But there's a subtle difference between Charles’ and my car, basically, just in the race. It's just to do mostly with flap, how much wing you put in, and I think we've just been under-hitting it – continuously under-hitting it for some reason.

“When you do the laps of the grid, it feels like the car is good. And then as soon as the race starts, it's just massive washout and understeer. I couldn't do anything about it, so they just pulled away. I lost those eight seconds, and that was really why I didn't get that [third] position in the end.”

title: Ford Fathom will be the cheapest American EV capable of powering a house
raw_summary: Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid. summary: Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid. The new chargers promise to be about half the cost of Ford’s existing equivalent products , which could make the technology available to more households.
article_paragraphs: Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.

The new chargers promise to be about half the cost of Ford’s existing equivalent products , which could make the technology available to more households. Ford said the Fathom itself will start at $28,350.

The Fathom will be capable of delivering “over 10 kW” to a home, Ford said. That would allow the electric vehicle to substitute for a small standby generator. For most U.S. homes, it wouldn’t be enough to power everything, but it could keep a refrigerator and air conditioner operational for about half a day.

Such capability has been touted as an advantage EVs have over fossil fuel vehicles, but not many EVs come properly equipped, and the chargers required to make use of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) services tend to be costly.

The Home Power Station device can help customers shave their utility bill by charging the Fathom when power prices are low and sending electricity back to the home when prices are high. The automaker says it will cost around $650, about 50% less than its first-generation bidirectional charger.

The other option, Home Backup Power, is a package that bundles the Home Power Station with a second device, the Home Backup Panel, to allow the Fathom to also power parts or all of a home when the power goes out. Ford says the package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first-generation product.

None of those prices include installation, which for existing V2X chargers can run up to $10,000, depending on how much electrical work needs to be done to prepare the home. Ford did not announce any partnerships with installers, though a spokesperson told TechCrunch that Ford would release more details at a later date.

Which loads the Fathom can power will vary by household and the specifics of each installation. Things like air conditioners and refrigerators, for example, typically require a large surge of power to start up, after which point their load drops. So-called soft-start devices can help mitigate the surge, though they add cost to the installation.

Gernot Döllner, CEO of Audi, took the stage with U.S. President Donald Trump at a campaign rally to announce the construction of a new factory . I asked at the time whether hitching your corporate wagon to a historically disliked politician who faces an all-time midterm rout was a good idea, but there was an angle I hadn't considered: What Audi's workers, based in Germany, would think. Turns out they're not huge fans, and they control enough of the company to make that a problem. From Automotive News :

BERLIN — Audi CEO Gernot Döllner's on-stage embrace of President Trump during the announcement of a new U.S. factory for the brand is drawing fierce criticism in Germany, handing unions new leverage over Volkswagen Group's restructuring plans.

Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ), one of Germany's leading newspapers, described Döllner's appearance alongside Trump as "Bending the Knee in Georgia." Other commentators labeled the Audi chief, a key ally of VW Group CEO Oliver Blume, a national embarrassment.

An investment of this scale must be approved by VW Group's supervisory board. Under Germany's co-determination laws, half of the board's seats are held by labor representatives, while VW Group's home state of Lower Saxony holds two seats.

Volkswagen is looking to shutter factories and lay off workers at home, but it suddenly has money for an all-new factory in the U.S. — all to appease a president who's not particularly loved by most. I'm no fancy big-city MBA, but I probably would've handled just about all of this differently.

See that up there? That's the GM EV1, a car that signaled General Motors' interest in exploring electrification back in the '90s. Yet, in the 30 years since that car's launch, both General Motors and the country in which it's based have largely rejected the EV — a stance that's increasingly making both company and country international pariahs. summary: Elon Musk says Tesla’s Robotaxi race against Waymo “was never a real contest” after Tesla’s driverless fleet logged 438,000 miles in Austin in a single week, edging past Waymo’s 406,000 weekly average in the city. That’s one city, one week, and a Waymo figure that’s four months old.
article_paragraphs: Elon Musk says Tesla’s Robotaxi race against Waymo “was never a real contest” after Tesla’s driverless fleet logged 438,000 miles in Austin in a single week, edging past Waymo’s 406,000 weekly average in the city.
That’s one city, one week, and a Waymo figure that’s four months old. Across the US, Waymo still drives about seven times more driverless miles than Tesla every week.

The chart going around comes from Robotaxi Tracker , a community project that pulls driverless mileage from each company’s own reports: Tesla’s weekly Robotaxi safety report and Waymo’s quarterly Safety Impact data hub.
Jason Scharf posted the Austin view on X with the comment that “the battle for Autonomous Austin might already be over.” Musk replied overnight: “It was never a real contest.”

The Austin data is real –albeit with some caveats. In the week ending October 18, Tesla reported 438,000 miles with no safety monitor aboard in Austin, up 30% from the week before. Waymo averaged about 406,000 miles a week in Austin in the second quarter.

But the tracker’s own caption explains the catch. Tesla’s figure is its latest week. Waymo’s is an average of April through June, because Waymo publishes about three months after each quarter ends. So Musk is comparing Tesla’s best week ever to Waymo’s spring.

Waymo averaged 3.90 million rider-only miles per week in Q2 2026. Tesla did 558,000 miles in its best week. Waymo’s Phoenix, Bay Area, and Los Angeles markets each drive more miles per week on their own than Tesla’s entire network.

Cumulative numbers are even more lopsided. Waymo has logged 271.3 million rider-only miles since 2020, including 50.7 million in Q2 alone, as we covered when Waymo released its latest safety data . Tesla has 3.11 million driverless miles since January 22, 2026. Waymo drove more than that in a single week.

article_paragraphs: Ford wants to make powering your home with an EV a lot cheaper. Its upcoming sub-$30,000 Fathom electric truck will feature a new bidirectional charging system that ditches the need for an expensive external inverter.
Arriving in 2027, the Fathom will be the first EV from a US automaker priced below $30,000 that can deliver more than 10 kW of AC power to a home without a separate wall-mounted inverter.
And Ford says it’s cutting the cost of the other equipment needed for home backup power, too.

EV batteries store electricity as direct current (DC), but our homes use alternating current (AC). To send power from an EV battery into a house, traditionally, that meant installing a pricey external inverter.
Ford has come up with a different approach for its new Universal EV Platform, which will underpin the Fathom.

After acquiring startup Auto Motive Power in 2023, Ford redesigned its bidirectional charging system from the ground up. Instead of relying on a separate wall-mounted inverter, it built one directly into the truck’s E-box, one of the vehicle’s five main modules.
Fewer parts mean lower costs, and Ford says the savings will extend to the home charging equipment, too.
Fathom owners will have two ways to use the truck’s battery to power their homes.

This was partly due to problems specific to this race, such as strategic decisions Verstappen was unhappy with – particularly the insistence on sticking with the softer compounds while the harder ones seemed to work better – and inconsistent behaviour from the power unit. But the difficult Sunday afternoon at the Circuit of the Americas was also caused by two problems that have repeatedly cropped up this year: poor starts and technical issues with the team radio.
All of this led to frustration for Isack Hadjar , who summed it up as follows in the media pen:“At the moment, it's the little things we can’t do.

"I have poor radio, I don't even know what's happening. And whenever I drop the clutch, it's going into a nightmare. If we fix these two issues, we might already be on the podium. It seems like we can do the hardest things, but we can’t do the silly things.”

By 'the hardest things', he was naturally referring to the fact that Red Bull has managed to overturn its enormous gap to the front of the field. In Australia, China and Japan, the average deficit in race pace was 1.2 seconds per lap, and making up that kind of ground over the course of a season is certainly no small feat.

At the same time, tackling the start problem and getting the radio issues under control has proved more complicated than expected. When Autosport put those observations to Laurent Mekies, referring to Hadjar's comments, the team principal clarified that the two aspects needed to be treated separately. Yes, the radio problem is unacceptable for a top team and must be resolved before the end of this year, but the start issue is more complex and will remain an obstacle until 2027.

“I guess there are two different ways to answer your question," said Mekies. “I think there is some truth in what Isack is saying, meaning that we are all frustrated to struggle with radio issues for the second race in a row. It's making everyone's lives very difficult, so it is true that it's something that we would like to fix quite quickly, because it's an item that should be working without using too much of our energy.
“So he's right on that one. The start is a slightly more complex issue to solve.”

Austin typified a bit of a running theme for Ferrari this year. Strong throughout practice, in contention early on in qualifying, underwhelming in Q3, recovering in the race but often leaving it too late to take the victory.
It is an assessment that team principal Fred Vasseur did not dispute.

"I think the weekend went well and everything is working as expected on the [upgrade] package ," he said. "But the issue is that we did all the laps, from the first lap of FP1 to the last lap of the race, in good shape except the last two laps of Q3 on both cars. It's probably where we missed something."

What the US GP highlighted for not just Ferrari but all those fighting at the front is that, if everything is not nailed perfectly, the consequences from losing the smallest amount of time in qualifying can define weekends.
Fourth and fifth on the grid for Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton was a disappointment in terms of the final positions and the impact that would then have on their hopes for the race.
Yet Hamilton's fifth-fastest time was just 0.097 seconds off what Max Verstappen had been able to deliver to put himself on the front row.

title: Forgotten Roadster: The Unusual 1964 Lightburn “Zeta Sports”
raw_summary: This is a 1964 Lightburn Zeta Sports, it’s a pint-sized roadster from Australia powered by a rear-mounted engine that drives the rear wheels through a 4-speed manual transmission. It’s believed that only 28-50 of these cars were ever made, and they remain largely forgotten today, even in Australia. It’s believed that only 28-50 of these cars were ever made, and they remain largely forgotten today, even in Australia.
article_paragraphs: This is a 1964 Lightburn Zeta Sports, it’s a pint-sized roadster from Australia powered by a rear-mounted engine that drives the rear wheels through a 4-speed manual transmission.

It’s believed that only 28-50 of these cars were ever made, and they remain largely forgotten today, even in Australia. It’s not known how many have survived, however some estimates put the number in the single digits.

Lightburn & Co was an Adelaide, Australia-based manufacturer of washing machines and cement mixers , so it might seem odd that they seemingly suddenly decided, in the early 1960s, to put their own sports car into production. The company had actually started out as a motor car repair garage that Albert Henry Lightburn opened behind his family home in the Adelaide suburb of Unley in 1919, so the automotive link had always been there.

The Lightburn Zeta Sports had its origins in the Frisky Sprint from England, which Gordon Bedson and his development engineer Keith Peckmore had developed at Henry Meadows Ltd in Wolverhampton. Bedson was a former Vickers aircraft engineer who had designed Stirling Moss’s 500cc Formula 3 car at Kieft. Image courtesy of Lightburn & Co.

Lightburn’s oldest son, Harold, had taken over the company after Albert died in October 1940 and, from 1941, moved it into manufacturing, starting with workshop equipment like Lightning hydraulic jacks. Washing machines followed in 1949, along with concrete mixers, and then fiberglass boats. Because why not.

The first of Harold Lightburn’s production cars to go on sale was the Zeta Runabout, a fiberglass sedan that launched in 1963 at £595 (about $1,330 USD). A 324cc Villiers two-stroke twin drove the front wheels, and there was no reverse gear – to back up, the driver stopped the engine, then restarted it running backwards, which allowed the regular forward gears to move it in reverse. It was a clever arrangement.

Zeta was the brand Lightburn used for all its cars, so the sedan was sold as the Zeta Runabout, the pickup as the Zeta Utility, and the roadster as the Zeta Sports. The timeline of the various model releases is a little haphazard, the Zeta Sports was developed first, but went on sale after the Zeta Runabout sedan and the Zeta Utility. No one is quite sure why, and the actual reason seems to be lost to history.

raw_summary: Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in a funding round that values the autonomous vehicle technology startup at $4.1 billion, marking a speedy ascent for the two-year-old company. The Series C round, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, comes two months after the startup reached a key milestone: moving its autonomous excavators beyond testing and pilot programs and putting them to work on active construction sites.

article_paragraphs: Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in a funding round that values the autonomous vehicle technology startup at $4.1 billion, marking a speedy ascent for the two-year-old company.

The Series C round, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, comes two months after the startup reached a key milestone: moving its autonomous excavators beyond testing and pilot programs and putting them to work on active construction sites.

Bedrock Robotics has developed a self-driving kit that can be retrofitted onto construction and other worksite vehicles. Excavators outfitted with Bedrock’s autonomous-driving tech are now commercially operating at a Nevada-based water treatment facility, an earthwork site run by Champion Site Prep in Texas , and a 1.2 million-cubic-yard civil sitework project with Zachry Construction Corporation.

Bedrock has raised nearly $1 billion since it was founded in 2024 by a group of autonomous vehicle and robotics industry veterans. Co-founder and CEO Boris Sofman previously led Waymo’s now-shuttered self-driving trucks program. Sofman also co-founded and led Anki Robotics, the maker of the popular Cozmo consumer robot, which shut down in 2019.

Other co-founders include Waymo veterans Kevin Peterson, Bedrock’s chief technology officer, and Ajay Gummalla, who serves as Bedrock’s vice president of engineering and infrastructure. Tom Eliaz, who previously worked at Segment and Twilio, is also a co-founder and VP of engineering and hardware.

The fresh capital will help Bedrock accelerate its transition to commercial work. The company plans to deploy its technology at more construction sites, while expanding the teams and infrastructure needed to support customers in the field.

“We have proven that fully autonomous excavators can perform real work of value alongside the crews and workflows already in place on job sites. The next challenge is delivering that capability to more contractors as a dependable part of how projects get built,” Sofman said in a statement.

Bedrock is particularly focused on autonomous excavators, in part because of a growing shortage of skilled operators. It takes five years or more to master operating an excavator, according to Bedrock. Meanwhile, a growing number of construction workers are approaching retirement age. The Associated Builders and Contractors, a national construction industry trade association, estimates that more than 40% of construction workers will retire in the next five years.

title: Why Hypoid Differential Gear Oil Needs To Be Different From Engine Or Transmission Oil
raw_summary: With all the fluids modern cars require, it's only natural to wonder whether one lubricant can handle multiple duties. Scratch hypoid gear oil off the list if you want the engine or most transmissions to keep functioning properly. We'll get to the reason shortly, but let's first explain how hypoid gearsets work. These gears, located in the differential between the rear (or sometimes front) wheels, are common on tow-oriented pickups and body-on-frame SUVs. Some all-wheel-drive vehicles also have a hypoid gear setup in the power transfer unit, which directs power back to the rear wheels. Originally called a hyperboloidal gear, hypoid is the modernized term for a setup where the pinion gear meets the ring gear offset from the center. The driveshaft sits below, lowering the center of gravity and opening up more floor space. However, the gear teeth rub against each other in a sliding motion that squeezes the lubricant away from the teeth, leaving the metal surfaces without a full oil film between them (known as boundary lubrication). A specialized lubricant with EP (extreme pressure) additives inside the oil protects the exposed metal once the oil film between the gear teeth is squeezed out. This kind of gear oil meant for hypoid differentials typically carries the American Petroleum Institute (API) GL-5 designation. Let's look at how it's different.
